newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices consolidate, confidence weak.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices consolidate, confidence weak.

text.p: China's A and B share indices consolidated on Friday after sharp falls over the past few days with continuing bearish sentiment keeping investors away from the markets, brokers said.

The Shanghai B share index edged up 0.449 points or 0.59 percent to 76.225 points despite a meeting to discuss ways to keep domestic investors out of the B share market, brokers in Shanghai said. The A index gained 0.76 percent to 1,211.447.

The Shenzhen B index lost 0.57 points or 0.42 percent to 135.40 and while A shares erased early losses to end up 3.36 points or 0.82 percent at 411.62 on a technical rebound, brokers in Shenzhen said.

"The B share market's recent poor performance coupled with shrinking turnover indicate weakening investor confidence," a trader at J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said. "It was a day dominated by volatile trading among small investors."
Analysts said stagnant trading would extend into early next week ahead of the listing of Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd, which is set to float 400 million B shares on the Shenzhen bourse next Tuesday.
They said the expected modest debut by Bengang due to weak market sentiment and limited optimism over China's steel industry is likely to further dampen confidence.
Brokers in Shanghai said the slight gains on the local bourse were just a technical rebound, and the future trend was still uncertain.

The B share regulatory meeting focused on implementation of existing rules banning domestic investors from trading in the B share market, but no new control measures for B share trading were discussed, they said.
"If the meeting had worked out some solid new measures to ban domestic investors from trading B shares, it would have had a negative impact on the market," a local broker said.
"In China, there is always lax enforcement in imposing government policies," the local broker said. "So I do not think the meeting could really shake the B share market."
Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington Glass Co was the best Shanghai B share performer, jumping $0.034 or 9.29 percent to $0.400 on volume of 99,500 shares.
Recently-listed Hainan Airlines Co was the most actively traded on domestic buying. It gained $0.010 or 1.92 percent to $0.530 on volume of 1.5 million shares.
On the Shenzhen B share market, the biggest loser was Shenzhen Textile, sinking HK$0.27 or 9.68 percent to HK$2.52 on volume of only 3,600 shares.
